thread.title: Warren Buffett’s big bet on Apple has one Wall Street trader asking: Has he lost it?

author: Shawn Langlois
title: Warren Buffett’s big bet on Apple has one Wall Street trader asking: Has he lost it?
text:
Published: Nov 5, 2018 1:13 p.m. ET Share Warren Buffett in his office in Omaha
By Social-media editor
Has Warren Buffett finally lost it?
The Brooklyn Investor, a website that regularly pops up on “best of” lists for value investing blogs, asked that very question in a post over the weekend.
The anonymous blogger — a self-described longtime Wall Street strategist and trader — has a problem with just how heavily weighted in Apple AAPL, -2.84% Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway BRK.A, +5.03% has become.
At a whopping $52 billion as of Nov. 4, Apple, the Brooklyn Investor points out, is by far Berkshire’s biggest position.
“Wow, that’s a big bet, exceeding 10% of the market cap of BRK,” he wrote. “I am not the biggest fan of AAPL, so it is interesting. Coming right off his IBM IBM, +3.80% miss, I guess many shareholders would be a little surprised.”
His main grievance is that Apple has been “chasing the crowd” instead of leading it or disrupting it like the company used to back in the glory days.
“Moving up to higher end products to make up for declining growth momentum reminds me of retailers/restaurants that hid declining traffic/unit volumes by moving up-market or raising prices,” he wrote. “It works for a while until people finally say, no mas, and will no longer pay high prices.”
While he doesn’t recommend it, the Brooklyn Investor says if others aren't feeling the heavily weighted position, they could just hedge their exposure by shorting Apple against holding Berkshire.
A timely bet against Apple before its disappointing earnings report last Thursday would have paid off nicely. The stock dropped 6.6% in Friday’s session, its worst single-day percentage drop since 2014 . This week hasn’t offered much relief, either. Apple was off another 4% at last check.
Meanwhile, Berkshire surged early Monday after the company revealed over the weekend better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and that it bought back stock for the first time in six years.
